philosophie.label: THE DE FACTO PHILOSOPHY
philosophie.title: A logical order, from diagnosis through to maintenance.

piliers.title: Understand before treating.
piliers.body: The right treatment follows from a clear diagnosis: its cause, its prognosis and the overall context of the mouth.

piliers.title: Stabilise before rebuilding.
piliers.body: A mouth is not rebuilt on unstable foundations: active disease is brought under control first.

piliers.title: Preserve before replacing.
piliers.body: Keep natural tissue where it can reasonably be kept — without saving everything at any cost, or replacing everything quickly.

piliers.title: Prevent to make it last.
piliers.body: Prevention is an active part of treatment, present from the very first appointment — never a formality at the end of the process.

studioSection.title: 728 rue Fleury Est, room by room
studioSection.intro: The operatories, the planning station and the laboratory are all under the same roof.

laboratoireSection.label: THE INTEGRATED LABORATORY
laboratoireSection.title: From diagnosis to fabrication, under one eye
laboratoireSection.intro: A complete dental laboratory, integrated into the clinic: restorations and appliances are designed, fabricated and adjusted on site — for full continuity between the clinical diagnosis and the delivered result.

blocs.title: Dental technologist on site
blocs.body: The same hands follow your case from beginning to end of the fabrication of appliances and restorations — with no anonymous outsourcing.

blocs.title: Direct communication
blocs.body: The dentist, the dental technologist and the patient discuss the same project without an intermediary: fewer back-and-forths, shade or shape adjustments made on site, and no instruction lost along the way.

blocs.title: Complete digital planning
blocs.body: The workflow is entirely digital — optical impression, design, fabrication — and every project is archived: if something breaks, a restoration can be reproduced identically from the original file.

laboratoireSection.cloture: Technology does not decide the treatment. It serves the diagnosis, the precision and the coherence of the clinical project.

parcoursSection.label: THE DE FACTO CARE PATHWAY
parcoursSection.title: Five stages, one common thread.
parcoursSection.intro: The pathway reads from diagnosis towards rehabilitation, but it is neither mandatory nor strictly linear. You can leave it, return to it, or stop at a stage. Only one thing runs through it from end to end: prevention.
parcoursSection.s3Note: Prevention accompanies every stage, for life
parcoursSection.pasLigneDroiteLabel: WHY IT IS NOT A STRAIGHT LINE
parcoursSection.pasLigneDroiteBody: The pathway depends on each person's diagnoses, risks and goals. Depending on the situation, you move forward, you pause, or you return to an earlier stage.
pasLigneDroitePoints: ↳ Branches and possible exits after stages 1, 2 or 3
↻ Reassessment points that may send you back to an earlier stage
◎ A maintenance loop that continues over the long term
parcoursSection.precisionLabel: A NOTE ON THE WORD STAGE
parcoursSection.precisionBody: In the [de facto] Pathway, a stage designates a family of therapeutic objectives. It does not represent the severity of a disease and does not mean that every patient must reach the next stage. Not to be confused with the stages of a periodontal classification, of a cancer, or with a severity grading.
parcoursSection.metaDescription: The [de facto] Pathway: five stages, from diagnosis to maintenance. De Facto Dental Studio, Ahuntsic, Montreal.
parcoursSection.optionsNote: Every option is quoted in writing before any commitment, with its risks and its alternatives — including those of doing nothing.

praticienVisite.portraitBody1: Born in Montreal, Dr Ramdani grew up in Saint-Michel and then in Ahuntsic. He studied dental medicine at Université Laval in Quebec City, before returning to practise in the neighbourhood where he grew up.
praticienVisite.portraitBody2: He founded De Facto Dental Studio to practise dentistry where diagnosis comes before intervention: understanding the mouth as a whole, explaining what is observed, and presenting options rather than a package.

colonne1.q: Do I need a referral for a first appointment?
colonne1.a: No. You can contact the studio directly, by phone, by email or with the online form.

colonne1.q: Is the studio accepting new patients?
colonne1.a: Yes. The first meeting is a complete examination, which serves as the starting point for everything else.

colonne1.q: How long does the first visit take?
colonne1.a: About 60 to 75 minutes, depending on the situation. That time covers the interview, the examination, the necessary images and the explanation of the clinical picture.
Monday to Wednesday, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

colonne1.q: What should I do in a dental emergency?
colonne1.a: Call the studio at 514 863 7805 during opening hours. We assess the situation and determine the appropriate timeframe.

colonne1.q: How do I get to the studio?
colonne1.a: The studio is at 728 rue Fleury Est, in Ahuntsic. The Sauvé and Henri-Bourassa metro stations are nearby and street parking is available.
Appointments, explanations and the documents provided are available in French and in English.

colonne2.q: Is the laboratory really on site?
colonne2.a: Yes. Design and fabrication take place in the digital laboratory integrated into the studio, by the same dental technologist, from beginning to end.

colonne2.q: Does the laboratory accept cases from other clinics?
colonne2.a: No. The laboratory is part of the studio and serves only the cases treated here.

colonne2.q: Is the studio affiliated with a group of clinics?
colonne2.a: No. The studio is independent: no corporate affiliation, no commercial partnership, no imposed sales targets.

colonne2.q: What do I receive after the examination?
colonne2.a: An explained clinical picture, a prioritised care plan provided in writing, the possible options and what happens if nothing is done.
Claims are submitted electronically to most insurers. A written estimate is provided before care begins.
The studio practises general dentistry, including interceptive orthodontics in children.

colonne2.q: Can I obtain my file or my radiographs?
colonne2.a: Yes. Your images and your file are provided on request, or sent to the professional of your choice.

intro.label: The Studio
intro.title: A dental studio designed to slow down, understand and plan better.
intro.body: De Facto Dental Studio was designed to offer a calmer, more structured and more personalized experience. The space, the clinical approach and the digital tools come together to create continuity between analysis, decision and treatment.

pourquoi.label: Why De Facto exists
pourquoi.title: Dr Ramdani's intention
pourquoi.body: De Facto Dental Studio grew out of Dr Ramdani's intention to create a different kind of care setting: a calm, precise and reassuring environment where the patient can be heard, understood and guided with clarity.
pourquoi.body2: The goal is not only to treat a tooth or respond to a symptom. The goal is to take the time to understand the patient's complete situation, explain what has been observed, plan care with judgment and set the right priorities.
pourquoi.body3: At De Facto, time, listening, precision and continuity are not details. They are the conditions for care that is better understood, better planned and more durable.
pourquoi.body4: The studio was designed to put the clinical relationship back at the centre of the experience: a place where technology supports the dentist's judgment without replacing it, and where every decision is made with measure.

philosophie.label: Clinical philosophy
philosophie.title: Understand before intervening
philosophie.body: Our philosophy rests on a simple idea: every treatment must fit within a global understanding of the patient. Before intervening, we seek to understand the risks, priorities, expectations and limits specific to each situation.

espace.label: The space
espace.title: A space designed to slow the pace
espace.body: The studio environment was designed to create a calmer, clearer and more human experience. Each zone — reception, clinical room, laboratory and discussion area — supports the same idea: take the time to do things well.

faq.label: Resources
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions. For anything else, our team is reachable directly.
faq.q1: Can I come in just for an emergency?
faq.a1: Yes, emergencies can be assessed based on availability. The goal of an emergency appointment is to assess the situation, provide relief when possible and determine next steps. A complete examination may be recommended afterward depending on the context.
faq.q2: Is a complete examination required for new patients?
faq.a2: To establish a structured clinical relationship and propose appropriate care, a complete examination is generally recommended for new patients. Some emergencies may, however, require a targeted assessment first.
faq.q3: How long does the first visit take?
faq.a3: For a complete examination alone, plan for 30 to 45 minutes. If a cleaning is combined with the same appointment, plan for at least 1 hour 15 minutes, depending on the clinical situation.
faq.a4: Not automatically. The cleaning may be performed during a combined or separate appointment depending on available time, gum condition, the amount of buildup and clinical needs.
faq.a5: We can assist you in transmitting certain information or estimates depending on the available systems. Coverage, limits and any uncovered balances remain the patient's responsibility.
faq.a6: Some care can be offered to children depending on age, cooperation and the clinical situation. When necessary, an appropriate referral may be recommended.
faq.a7: Yes, certain alignment cases can be assessed. When the situation falls outside appropriate indications, an orthodontic referral may be recommended.
faq.q8: Do you perform root canal treatments?
faq.a8: Certain endodontic treatments can be assessed or performed depending on the situation. Complex cases may be referred to an endodontic specialist.
faq.a9: Yes. When a situation falls outside the scope of treatment offered at the studio, we coordinate the referral to an appropriate specialist.
faq.q10: Will I receive a treatment plan?
faq.a10: Depending on the situation, a plan may be discussed immediately or presented at a separate appointment called the oral health portrait.
faq.q11: Can I send my radiographs in advance?
faq.a11: Yes, if you have recent radiographs or relevant documents, they can be sent to the team before or after booking an appointment.

sections.title: Information collected
sections.body: We collect the information needed for your care: identification, contact details, medical and dental information relevant to the safety and quality of care.

sections.title: Use of information
sections.body: Your information is used to organize appointments, maintain the clinical record, deliver care, follow up and communicate as needed for your care.

sections.title: Sharing of information
sections.body: Your information is only shared when necessary for care, for a referral to another professional, for collaboration with the laboratory, or when required by law.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Reasonable technical and organizational measures are in place to protect your information against loss, unauthorized access, modification or unintended disclosure.

sections.title: Access and correction
sections.body: You may request access to your information or correction of inaccurate details. An identity check may be required before processing the request.

sections.title: Consent
sections.body: Your consent is required to transmit certain information or documents (specialist referral, transmission to the laboratory, electronic communications). You may withdraw your consent for purposes not essential to care.

sections.title: Electronic communication
sections.body: Communications by email, SMS or web form may involve risks inherent to digital transit. The information transmitted should be limited to what is necessary for the request. For particularly sensitive information, an in-person or phone exchange may be preferable.

sections.title: Person responsible for the protection of personal information
sections.body: For any question regarding privacy, access to or correction of your personal information, or data security, you may contact the De Facto Dental Studio's person responsible for the protection of personal information by phone or email. De Facto Dental Studio operates under the laws applicable in Quebec and Canada, in particular the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25) and PIPEDA at the federal level.

blocs.texte: Dr Bader Ramdani, general dentist, born in Montreal. A 2021 doctor of dental medicine from Université Laval in Quebec City, he is a member of the Ordre des dentistes du Québec. He founded Studio De Facto in Ahuntsic, with a denture workshop on site, to give himself the time to examine, to explain and to treat. He sees patients in French and in English.
The studio team welcomes you, calls you back to confirm your appointments, helps you with your insurance and stays with you from one visit to the next.
Every complete examination ends with a written oral health report that you keep. It is the starting point for your decisions and your follow-up.
The studio gives free oral health workshops with neighbourhood community organizations.
